sections.html:
Salem is a harbor city in Essex County on the North Shore, about 15 miles northeast of downtown Boston. The 2020 population was 44,480, spread over 18.3 square miles, and more than half of that area is water. Salem is mostly a residential and tourist city, and Salem State University, with more than 10,000 students, adds steady rental activity.

Salem Harbor, the North and South rivers and the Danvers River cut the city into small pieces. A house a few blocks away across a river can feel like a different neighborhood to a buyer, so say plainly which part of town yours is in.

  • Downtown: the historic core of the city.
  • Salem Neck and Winter Island: a peninsula northeast of downtown, home to the 30-acre Winter Island Park.
  • North Salem: west of the Neck, across the North River.
  • South Salem: south of the South River, mostly along Salem Harbor.

Beverly, Danvers, Peabody, Lynn, Swampscott and Marblehead all touch the city line. Public parks, harbor frontage and water leave limited land for new building, which keeps the supply of houses small.

Few Massachusetts cities carry as much preservation weight. Salem was a leading seaport in early American trade, and the 1692 witch trials still define its public image. The Federal Street District and the Charter Street Historic District are two of its historic residential areas, and Chestnut Street is known for Federal architecture.

The Great Salem Fire of 1914 destroyed more than 400 homes and left 3,500 families homeless, yet it spared the Chestnut Street block of Federal houses. The result is a mix of very old streets beside neighborhoods rebuilt in the early 1900s.

If your house is in an historic district, ask the city's planning office before you plan exterior changes or a teardown, and tell buyers what you learn. A short list of dates for the roof, heating system and wiring also saves questions later.

sections.h2: Getting in and out of Salem
sections.html:
Salem has its own station on the MBTA Commuter Rail's Newburyport/Rockport Line. Routes 1A, 114 and 107 pass through the city, and Route 1A crosses the bridge to Beverly.

No highway runs inside the city. The closest access to Route 128 is along Route 114 in Peabody. Put that in a listing early, since some buyers assume an exit is close by.

A former rail line toward Marblehead is now a bike path, and the city has talked about a possible South Salem rail station on Ocean Avenue West. If your house is a short walk from the train, lead with that.

sections.h2: What are Salem's short-term rental rules?
sections.html:
Salem regulates short-term rentals more tightly than most Massachusetts cities, which matters if your house has ever been listed on Airbnb or a similar site. The City of Salem short-term rental page explains the ordinances the City Council adopted in 2018. They require:

  • Annual registration of the rental with the city.
  • A Certificate of Fitness.
  • For a property that is not the owner's primary residence, a special permit from the Zoning Board of Appeals and registration for the non-owner-occupied trash fee.
  • Collection of the state and local room occupancy excise tax.

New non-owner-occupied short-term rentals are not permitted. The special permit path covers only properties that were already operating as short-term rentals before July 16, 2018, and zoning limits the use to certain neighborhoods.

That rule can decide what a buyer is allowed to do with the house. If you bought it as a short-term rental, confirm its registration and permit status with the city before you list, and have the paperwork ready for the buyer's attorney.

sections.h2: Before closing: alarm certificate and deed tax
sections.html:
Massachusetts requires a certificate of compliance from the local fire department showing that smoke and carbon monoxide alarms meet the rules for a sale or transfer. Call the fire department as soon as you have a closing date. Alarms with no date stamp count as expired, and the department charges a fee. Details are on the Mass.gov alarm page.

The deed excise tax comes from G.L. c. 64D, section 1, which sets a base rate of $2 for each $500 of consideration. Your closing attorney will confirm the amount and who pays it.

For tax due dates, read the dates printed on your bill or call the assessor's office.

sections.h2: How to contest your Salem assessment
sections.html:
A tax abatement is a reduction granted when your house's fair cash value is lower than its assessed value. Valuation is set as of January 1 before the fiscal year. State law sets a short path:

  1. Pay your tax installments on time.
  2. File the approved abatement application with the assessors by the first installment due date on your bill.
  3. The assessors have three months to act, and silence counts as a denial.
  4. Appeal to the Appellate Tax Board within three months of the decision.

The Appellate Tax Board publishes a guide that walks through each step. Recent sales of similar nearby houses are the best evidence to bring.

sections.h2: What are your choices if you want to sell quickly?
sections.html:
You can list the house, sell it on your own, or accept a cash offer. A listing suits a house in good shape in a sought-after area. A cash sale suits a house that needs repairs, an inherited property or a landlord who wants out.

Salem adds a few items that can slow things down: a historic district review for exterior work, a short-term rental permit question, or a delay getting the alarm certificate from the fire department. Spot them early and you can pick the route that avoids the slowest steps.

With a cash offer, the buyer looks at the address, the condition and any liens or taxes, then makes an offer. If you accept, a title company or attorney handles the paperwork and the closing date is set around your timeline. There is no showing schedule, no repair list and no wait for a buyer's loan approval. Compare any offer with what you would keep after agent fees, repairs and months of carrying costs, and read the contract before you sign.

faqs.q: What county is Salem, MA in?
faqs.a: Salem is in Essex County, on the North Shore of Greater Boston.

faqs.q: Is there a highway in Salem?
faqs.a: No. The nearest Route 128 access is along Route 114 in neighboring Peabody.

faqs.q: Can I run a short-term rental in Salem?
faqs.a: Only with city registration, a Certificate of Fitness and, for a non-owner-occupied unit, a special permit. New non-owner-occupied short-term rentals are not permitted.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke and CO certificate to sell in Salem?
faqs.a: Yes. Massachusetts requires a local fire department certificate of compliance for the sale or transfer of a home.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Salem house in an historic district?
faqs.a: Yes. Ask the city's planning office before you plan exterior changes, and tell buyers about any review that applies.
